text: Five lessons, five moves -- and really, one repeatable process. This lesson pulls Chapter 3 together before Chapter 4 adds a piece that comes before all of it.

Lessons 11 and 12 turned vague complaints into working designs, one threshold-driven, one deadline-driven. Lesson 13 made sure that design survives the builder leaving. Lesson 14 had you run the whole method yourself. Lesson 15 made sure 'it works' actually means something.

Written out as one method: translate the complaint into requirements, design the automation, document it, test it across all four categories, and only then ship it. Skipping straight to shipping is exactly how undocumented, untested automation happens in the first place.

Run this health-check against any existing automation. Does a written requirement exist? Can you state the entry criteria without opening Setup? Is there a named owner with a last-reviewed date? Has it actually been tested, or only run once successfully?

Every case study in this chapter used a fictional company, but the method doesn't change when the company is real. Complaint to requirements to design to documentation to testing -- that's ordinary day-to-day admin work, not an advanced special case.
Chapter 3 assumed you already had a clear requirement to design against. Chapter 4 backs up one step: how do you actually gather that requirement from a stakeholder in the first place?
